title: One Pawn, Two Knights
setup: Both black knights are attacking your pawn on d3, and only the rook on d1 guards it. The pawn has a better idea than waiting.
hint: A pawn attacks the two squares diagonally ahead of it. Where would this one have to stand to attack c5 and e5?
explanation:
## The Idea

{{d4}} puts the pawn between the knights, attacking c5 and e5 at once. Neither knight can take it, because a knight on c5 or e5 never touches d4, and the rook on d1 guards it anyway.

Black saves one knight and the pawn takes the other: one point of pawn for three points of knight. Any other move lets both knights live.
